{"m": "gpt-4o", "msg": [{"content": "You compare short personal anecdotes by their underlying relational structure - the pattern of intentions, causes, deceptions, reversals, and outcomes among the people involved - NOT by their surface topic, setting, or vocabulary. Two stories can be about totally different situations yet share the same deep structure; two stories can share the same topic yet have opposite structure.", "role": "system"}, {"content": "SITUATION:
My housemate insists she 'doesn't understand how' to load the dishwasher properly—dishes always come out dirty when she tries. She has a Ph.D. in mechanical engineering. After six months of redoing her loads, I just started doing all the dishes. She thanked me for being 'so understanding.'

CANDIDATE A:
My housemate genuinely couldn't get our temperamental dishwasher to work at first—her loads kept coming out dirty. She asked me to show her the pre-rinse trick and how to stack the bottom rack. After a few tries she had it, and now she loads it better than I do.

CANDIDATE B:
The junior associate claimed he couldn't figure out the expense reporting system despite multiple trainings. I covered his reports for a year. Then I saw his freelance consulting profile advertising expertise in 'corporate financial systems implementation.' He'd been billing clients to set up the same software.

Which candidate shares the same underlying relational structure as the SITUATION (ignore surface topic similarity)? Respond as JSON: {"choice": "A" or "B", "reason": "<one sentence>"}.", "role": "user"}], "t": 0.0, "tag": "exp2:29"}
content: {"choice": "B", "reason": "Both involve someone feigning incompetence to avoid responsibility while possessing the capability to perform the task."}
